privacy_review: No evidence file is offered to readers. The body describes the saved manifests, config blobs and model-repository responses as a private author-side verification set and explicitly says they are not a downloadable dataset, so the new all-layer column carries no reader-facing file promise; receipt.public_artifacts stays empty by design. The only reusable artifact offered is the inline reader script, which the round-1 reviewer executed. The research brief, the review report and the fetched third-party documents remain private.
limitations: bpw is a size accounting only. No accuracy, perplexity, latency or memory-bandwidth measurement exists, so the Q8_0 trade-off stays unanswered (the article says so in 'What this does not tell you').

13 of 14 tags were never downloaded on this host; the single local cross-check (qwen2.5:0.5b) was made on 2026-11-02, a day before the 2026-11-03 registry audit window, so it confirms the local blob matches the registry today, not that the same bytes were present at audit time.
Registry tags can be re-pointed. The numbers are scoped to the 14 manifest digests recorded in the fetch log and re-confirmed unchanged at 00:42Z on 2026-11-03; a reader must re-run the script.

The table's printed fetch window 00:22:44Z-00:22:50Z covers the 14 manifest reads only (00:22:44.750Z-00:22:50.698Z); the 14 config-blob reads that supply file_type ran 00:22:51.102Z-00:22:58.689Z. The same section's separate '47 reads / 18.14 s' figure does cover the whole run (00:22:44.750Z-00:23:02.892Z), which was re-verified against the save log.

The nominal 4.85 bpw for Q4_K_M is the article's own blend of Q4_K (4.5) and Q6_K (6.5625), not a published per-file constant; the article frames it as 'roughly' and publishes the observed 4.649-6.442 spread.

The all-layer column sums manifest layers only and excludes the config blob (144-490 bytes) and the manifest itself, so 'ollama pull' transfers a few hundred bytes more than the printed total; the paragraph states the column is the layer sum.
The '64 GB at bf16' figure is a nominal 2 bytes x 32B; the repository total implies 65.5 GB.

Only one tag per family/quant combination was sampled; per-tensor quantization layouts were not inspected, so the mechanism offered for the +5.23%/+7.33% rows is labelled as expected rather than proven.
